page_title: Why Hazard Pointers Should be in C++26

sources.entry: Hazard Pointers for C++26 - The standard-track form of safe reclamation, fixing when a retired node may be freed while a reader still holds it.

summary.title: Hazard Pointers for C++26 (P2530R3)
summary.one_liner: You learn the proposed C++26 hazard pointer interface and wording for safe deferred memory reclamation, with its rationale and usage examples.
keywords: how to free memory safely while readers use it
takeaways: A hazard pointer is a single-writer multi-reader pointer; readers protect objects by setting it, and retired objects are reclaimed only when no hazard pointer points to them.
The proposal is a subset of the Concurrency TS 2 interface, omitting custom domains and global/cohort-based synchronous reclamation.
The interface centers on hazard_pointer_obj_base::retire, make_hazard_pointer, and hazard_pointer::protect/try_protect/reset_protection.
The reference implementation is Facebook's Folly library, reported in production use since 2017, with typical hazard_pointer construction/destruction around 4 ns.
summary.summary: This WG21 paper proposes adding hazard pointers, a safe deferred reclamation technique, to the C++26 standard, based on the Facebook Folly implementation used in production since 2017. It explains the rationale for a reduced subset of the Concurrency TS 2 interface, what was left out (custom domains, synchronous cohort reclamation) and why, and ABI-stability guidance. It walks through the protection and deferred reclamation mechanism, with read-mostly data, iterator, and singly-linked list examples comparing code with and without hazard pointers. The final section gives the proposed standard wording for the hazard_pointer_obj_base, hazard_pointer classes and their member functions.
